newsitem.title: RUSSIA: INTERVIEW-Uzbekistan Airways buying Western planes.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Uzbekistan Airways buying Western planes.

text.p: Uzbekistan Airways, the flagship carrier of one of the most conservative states to emerge from the Soviet Union, has begun modernising its fleet with Western aircraft, the chief executive said on Wednesday.
"We have a big Soviet fleet of (318) passenger planes and freighters and 56 helicopters, but many of them are outdated and must be replaced," Arslan Ruzmetov told Reuters.
The Russian aviation industry could not offer aircraft which the Central Asian carrier needs, he said. "It's the main reason we are acquiring Western-made planes."
Uzbekiston Havo Yullari (Uzbekistan Airways) will buy three Aero International (Regional) 85-passenger RJ-85 planes by the end of this year and two more next year, Ruzmetov said.
Last month the company made a firm order to buy an Airbus Industrie A-310 jet for delivery in May 1998. It began leasing two other A-310s four years ago and plans to buy them outright soon.
"It is more profitable than making leasing payments," Ruzmetov said.
The company bought three Boeing Co 767-300s in 1996 with Uzbek government financial backing.
"Without the government help, we could not modernise the fleet," Ruzmetov said, adding that the company earned only $6 million net profit in 1996 after years of losses.
The carrier, formerly a regional division of Aeroflot before the break-up of the USSR, has seen passenger volume recover to two million in 1996 from 900,000 in 1993. Volume was seven million in 1990.
Currently, Uzbekistan Airways operates scheduled flights from Tashkent to 20 countries.
Ruzmetov also said that the company planned to set up a technical service centre to cover all kinds of repair and service works of Western-made aircraft.
"We are ready to invest money in this project because Central Asian states operate such planes," he said.
